title: Castle v4: the Great Keep
status: approved by the owner on October 3 (the decision page): every part makes structural sense, every building inside fits its outside, the moat rings all four sides, the rock edges are natural with the built work on them, and the great hall and the chapel take steep slate roofs; design only, nothing built yet

curtain.note: One rectangle, symmetric about the main axis, standing in the moat on all four sides; wall walk at +7.06 between crenellated parapets. Every tower projects outward into the moat, so the inside faces stay straight and the buildings, gardens and yards stand right against them (no slots between a building and the wall). The north runs meet the keep's flanks square, between its turrets, and the walk enters the keep at its gallery level, which is the walk's own level.

runs.note: meets the keep's west wall square, 2.5 m clear of its back turret; the walk goes in by a door into the keep's west gallery at +7.06
its mirror, into the east gallery

curtain.north_range: the kitchen, the great hall, the chapel and the solar are built against the north runs: the walk runs along their back walls, which rise above it on its inner side
curtain.wall_walk_access: two stairs reach the walk: the spiral stairs in the gatehouse's drums (a door at the foot of each, facing the forecourt) and the keep's own stairs (its galleries open onto the north runs). The walk is one loop through every tower.
curtain.tower_doors: the walk passes through every tower: a door on each side at the walk's level, set square to the walk in a flat reveal cut back into the drum, its sill on the walk's deck and its head under the tower's first string course; never cut slantwise into the curve or half hidden by a parapet (owner-oct3-tower.png)

tower_spacing: west and east faces: a corner tower, three wall towers at the quarter points (19.75 m apart on the wall's line) and a corner tower; the south face: corner, wall tower, gatehouse, wall tower, corner, about 21 to 23 m apart; the keep breaks the north face. Every tower stands on the moat's bed, its plinth rising from the water.

gatehouse.note: today's gatehouse unchanged, moved onto the new axis: two D-towers 6 either side, a passage 4 wide under the ceremonial arch, the block a storey over the curtain, flags on the drums and the lord's banner over the arch. Its drums stay flat so the keep's spires rise over the gate front seen from below the rock. The drums stand on the moat's bed; the bridge lands between them at the passage's threshold.
gatehouse.doors: each drum has a door at its foot facing the forecourt, its spiral stair climbing to the wall walk (+7.06) and on to the drum's platform

keep.note: A massive square keep on the axis. Its front half stands on the raised terrace; its back half stands on the crown outside the north curtain, its back wall 4.9 m beyond the curtain, standing in the moat: the water passes behind it in a basin 5 m clear of its back turrets, and its back half rises straight out of the water on a battered plinth founded on the moat's rock bed, as the towers do. The north runs of the curtain meet its flanks square, between its turrets. Four round corner turrets rise a stage above its parapet to blue spires; a projecting frontispiece on the axis carries the great door and the showpiece window between two slender pinnacles.

water.note: Two springs break out of the rock behind the keep, through arched spouts in the moat's north bank. The moat rings all four sides at one level, 2 m below the turf, held there by a weir: the water runs round both sides of the castle to the axis under the gate terrace, slips over the weir into an arched culvert, runs south under the terrace and pours from an arch in the bastion's face as one fall to the pool at the rock's foot, from which the stream runs on to the pond. A sluice in the west arm's outer bank, its sill at the same level, feeds today's west fall off the brink into the Veil. Behind the keep the moat widens into a basin, so the keep's back rises straight out of the water like the towers; a rim of natural rock 3 to 4 m wide carries the north bank, the crown grown north for it.

water.level_logic: two springs in behind the keep, two outlets at one sill level (-2.0): the weir under the gate terrace takes almost all of it, the west sluice the rest, so the moat stands 2 m below the turf and 2.2 m deep whatever the springs bring; the water runs round both arms from the basin to the weir, so none of it stands still

approach.note: From the portal court the ore lane runs west along the foot of the castle rock to the foot of the climb under its south-east corner. The climb is a stone stair of four flights of 17 steps: two north between walls to a turning landing against the rock, two west along the rock face to the ledge, 11 m in all. Two lamp pillars stand at its head. The ledge road runs west between two walls, the moat below the inner one and the cliff below the outer one, to the gate terrace on the axis, where a bridge of two stone arches crosses the moat to the gate. East of the stair's head the landing is a walled terrace over the court; west of the gate terrace the ledge walk runs between the same two walls to the lookout, so the south front balances about the gate. The inner wall is straight, on the moat's coping; the outer wall follows the rock's natural brink in straight runs a pier to a pier, so the ledge is wider here and narrower there, a strip of turf between the paved way and the outer wall where the rock swells. Everything from the stair's head to the gate is level with the crown.
approach.levels: world heights: the court, the ore lane and the stair's foot at 0; the ledge, the landing, the gate terrace, the bridge and the gate at 11

gate_terrace.note: the middle of the ledge widened into a bastion that projects 2.5 m beyond the natural brink: its west, south and east faces are battered masonry founded on the rock at the cliff's foot, carrying the parapet; the culvert runs under it and the fall pours from the arch in its south face; two lamps, two banner poles at the bridge's foot

bridge.note: two segmental stone arches, one pier in the middle of the moat founded on its bed (pointed cutwaters east and west, where the water comes from), the south abutment the gate terrace's bank over the culvert, the north end landing at the gate's threshold between the drums; parapets both sides ending on piers

climb.note: A stone stair of four straight flights, each of 17 risers of 16.2 cm and 16 treads of 30 cm (a 28 degree stair, two risers and a tread making 62 cm), 3.6 m wide, with level landings between them. Flights 1 and 2 climb north from the ore lane between two walls to the turning landing at +5.5, which stands against the rock's south-east corner; flights 3 and 4 climb west along the rock face, the rock on their right and a wall on their left, to the head at +11, where the ledge road's outer wall opens between two lamp pillars. The whole stair is solid masonry: its flights and landings are filled and paved, its walls are its retaining walls, so nothing spans a gap. Every wall's coping follows its flight's pitch and runs level over the landings, with a pier at every change.

crown.note: The crown grows to carry the moat all round and the ledge: north far enough that a rim of rock 3 to 4 m wide carries the moat's north bank behind the keep, west and east to about x 21 and 132, south to the ledge's natural brink. Its edge is natural mossy rock, never a ruled line: it wanders a metre or two in and out, swells into a knoll at the south-west corner (the lookout) and round the landing at the south-east. Its outline stays inside the island's everywhere. Only the gate bastion and the climb are built masonry; where the climb's last two flights run along the rock, the rock face is dressed straight (z 116) so the stair's fill bears against it.

owner_notes.answer: a simple plan for each building (castle-v4-interiors.png and interiors): every door one door from both sides at one level, every window lighting a room, every chimney over a hearth, every upper floor with its stair; this moved the keep's second floor up to +20 so the great door and the showpiece window rise clear in the hall, made the stables and barracks 2 m deeper and 0.5 m taller so stalls flank an aisle and a loft clears the 4 m doors, and centred the hall's lantern on its hearth

owner_notes.note: October 3, on the plan: the water moat should go around the back too
owner_notes.answer: the moat rings all four sides: behind the north curtain and round the keep's back, which now rises out of the water on its plinth; the crown and the island grow up to 4.5 m north so a rim of rock carries the north bank; the springs move behind the keep and the water runs round both sides to the weir

owner_notes.note: October 3, on the plan: the ledge walk, the lookout and the rock edge around them should be more naturally shaped
owner_notes.answer: the crown's edge is natural rock all round (west, north, east and the south brink); the lookout sits on a knoll with its wall following the rim; the ledge's outer wall follows the brink in straight runs with a turf verge where the rock swells; the landing follows the east brink; only the gate bastion and the climb stay squared, as built masonry

owner_notes.note: October 3, roofs: pick B, steep blue slate roofs as in the painting on the great hall and the chapel
owner_notes.answer: the hall and the chapel get steep slate roofs (52 degrees, eaves +12, ridge +20.9) with the hall's lantern and the chapel's flèche on the ridges; their north gutters stay behind parapets over the wall walk; the kitchen and the solar keep flat roofs behind battlements as the range's low ends, so the range climbs from battlements to slate to the keep

structural_review.check: every rise on the way in is a stair or a gentle road
structural_review.how: the only rise between the court and the gate is the climb, 11 m in four flights of 17 steps with level landings; the ore lane, the landing, the ledge, the gate terrace and the bridge are all level

outdoors the hero stands on the cell levels, smoothed between cell centres, so each flight is walked as an even slope at its pitch (0.54 m up per 1 m cell) with the steps drawn on it; landings are flat; every outdoor stair is at least 3.6 m (three cells) wide between its walls; the walls are blocked cells. Inside, stairs change floor at their foot and head with a fade, as today

structural_review.check: every terrace edge is a retaining wall
structural_review.how: the upper court's edge (2 m, with its balustrade), the keep's podium, the gate bastion's faces, the stair's walls and the moat's outer bank are all dressed retaining walls; the ledge's outer wall stands on a masonry facing that caps the rock

structural_review.check: every drop has a wall or a parapet
structural_review.how: the ledge road, the walk, the landing, the lookout, the gate terrace, the bridge and every flight and landing of the climb are walled on every open side; the terrace has its balustrade; the wall walk and every tower top their parapets; the keep's galleries and the minstrels' gallery a balustrade along their open sides; the rims outside the moat are shut off by the landing's and the lookout's walls

structural_review.check: every bridge stands on arches or piers that reach water or rock
structural_review.how: the gate bridge is two stone arches on one pier founded on the moat's bed, abutting the gate terrace and the gate's threshold; the culvert under the terrace is vaulted

structural_review.check: the moat has built banks, a held level and an outfall
structural_review.how: dressed outer bank with a coping all the way round; the curtain, the towers and the keep's back half rise from the water on plinths; the springs feed the basin behind the keep and the water runs round both arms to the weir; the weir and the west sluice share one sill at -2, so the water stands 2 m below the turf; it leaves by the culvert and the fall to the pool and the stream

structural_review.check: every door opens onto a floor or a stair at its own level
structural_review.how: the north range and the keep open onto the terrace at +2; the stables and barracks onto the yards at 0; the gatehouse's drum doors onto the forecourt at 0; the tower doors and the keep's gallery doors onto the wall walk at +7.06 (the keep's galleries are now at the walk's level)

structural_review.check: every wall walk and tower is reached by a stair
structural_review.how: the gatehouse's drum stairs and the keep's stairs reach the walk, which runs through every tower; the towers' platforms and the keep's turrets have their own stairs

structural_review.check: no building or tower over a void or half on rock
structural_review.how: the towers, the drums and the keep's back half stand on the moat's bed; the moat's north bank on a rim of rock 3 m wide or more; the gate bastion and the stair on the rock at the cliff's foot; the ledge's outer walls on the brink; the crown's outline lies inside the island's everywhere
the north range, the stables and the barracks stand against the curtain; the gardens and yards run to it; no garden wall or fence stands in front of the curtain

structural_review.check: every building's inside fits its outside
structural_review.how: see interiors: rooms inside the walls, each door the same door from both sides at one floor level, each window within one storey and lighting a room, chimneys over hearths, the hall's lantern over its hearth, every loft or upper floor with a stair and headroom, no door taller than the floor over it

structural_review.check: every roof sheds its water somewhere it can go
structural_review.how: the slate roofs' south eaves drip onto the terrace's paving; their north slopes drain into parapet gutters over the wall walk that spout through the curtain into the moat; the flat roofs fall to spouts in their parapets; no gutter empties onto a walk or a door

structural_changes: the climb: today's sloping deck becomes a stone stair of four flights with landings (a 1 in 3 slope is no road and a deck needs something under it)
the ledge road gets a wall on its moat side as well as on the cliff (owner's note)

the north curtain moves 3 m south (z 18 to 21) so it meets the keep's flanks square instead of running half into its back turrets; the keep's galleries move to the walk's level so the walk walks straight in

the north range, the stables and the barracks are built against the curtain (there were 0.9 m slots behind them); the terrace, gardens and yards run to the curtain; the garden walls and paddock fences that stood in front of it go
the terrace's garden stairs get the grand stair's risers (12 of 17 cm) instead of 8 steep steps; the keep's inner stairs get two flights of 15 risers instead of a 5 m ladder
the bridge is two arches on a pier on the moat's bed; the drawbridge goes
the moat gets one sill level for its two outlets, so its water level is fixed
the landing and the lookout are no longer rectangles of rock sticking out of the cliff (rock does not grow square); only the gate bastion projects, and it is built masonry
the crown is drawn inside the island everywhere: the north-east corner pulled in, the island's south-west notch filled (the lookout hung over the void)
tower doors on the walk sit square in flat reveals at the walk's level

the keep's throne hall rises to the great chamber's floor at +20 and its galleries stop short of the south wall, so the 8 m great door and the showpiece window no longer pass through a gallery or a floor
the keep's front turrets hold its spiral stairs (their stepping slit lights face the bailey), reached from the hall stairs' half landings

the stables and the barracks are 10 m deep (were 8) and 7 m to their parapets (were 6.5): stalls either side of an aisle, and a loft at +2.9 over the stalls, the 4 m gable doors standing in bays open to the roof
the hall's lantern moves 2.25 m east over its hearth; the kitchen's and the solar's chimneys stand on their hearths

the moat rings the north side too: the keep's back half and the north curtain rise out of it, the crown grows north so the north bank stands on a rim of rock, and the springs move from the arms' head walls (which go) to the north bank behind the keep

the crown's edge is natural rock instead of ruled lines; the ledge's outer walls, the lookout's and the landing's follow the brink in straight runs with a pier at every angle; the gate bastion is the one squared projection, and it is built
the great hall and the chapel are roofed in slate on stone-coped gables with gutters behind a parapet over the wall walk; the hall's lantern and the chapel's flèche stand on their ridges

build_stages.name: ground plan
build_stages.what: the castle's plan moves out of buildKeep into its own module split by area (plan constants, ground and water, approach, bailey dressing, building specs) so later stages edit separate files; the new axis, curtain (north runs at z 21), towers, gatehouse position, the terrace platform with built edges, moat cells, crown and island outline, the approach's levels (the ledge level with the crown; each flight of the climb graded at its pitch with flat landings, its cells reserved so the cliff pass never turns them to rock; today's ramp removed), the farm and stream moves; today's kit placed at the new positions (curtain, drum towers, gatehouse, fountain, parterre), the keep and the wings as plain enterable buildings in today's style; tests (symmetry, connected walks, walkable flights, geometry audit) and the inspect views updated

build_stages.name: the great keep
build_stages.what: its own model, its back half on a battered plinth out of the moat: frontispiece, pinnacles, showpiece window, storey-by-storey windows, machicolated parapet, four turrets with stair lights and spires, great door, banners, great flag; interior: throne hall to +20, dais, piers, two stairs with doors into the front turrets' spirals, galleries on three sides; the north range opens as one round the hero

build_stages.name: moat and water
build_stages.what: moat surface on all four sides, its dressed outer bank and coping, the basin behind the keep, the springs in its north bank, the weir, culvert and outlet arch, the south fall and pool, the west sluice, channel and fall, the stream's new head and the viewing bay; the crown's natural edge

build_stages.name: approach and gate front
build_stages.what: the climb's stair (flights with nosings, landings, walls whose copings rake with each flight and step level over the landings, piers, buttresses, lamps), the ledge road and walk between their two walls (the outer one following the brink, the turf verge), the landing and the lookout on the knoll, the gate bastion (battered masonry faces, parapets, banner poles, lamps), the bridge (two arches on a pier, parapets)
files: src/world/approach props (new: stair flight, raking wall, parapet run, bridge arch)
the approach part of the castle plan module

build_stages.name: bailey grounds
build_stages.what: the narrower parterre, the walled kitchen and privy gardens (walls, gates, beds, well, basin, arbour), stable and muster yards, paddock and training yard (fences, gates, pells, butts, horses), trees, lamps, kerbs
files: the bailey dressing part of the castle plan module

build_stages.name: the other buildings
build_stages.what: the great hall (today's range turned round), the kitchen moved, the chapel and the solar (slate roofs on coped gables for the hall and the chapel, the lantern and the flèche on their ridges, gutters behind the north parapets), the stables and barracks; each its own window scheme; each built inside to its plan in interiors (rooms, doors from both sides, stairs, hearths)

build_stages.name: carried details
build_stages.what: champion helmets, fewer gold diamonds, long banners, the dragon's forelegs, clear tinted glass (with the stone work)

build_stages.name: together
build_stages.what: CASTLE_DESIGN.md, the inspect suite's views, the owner's picture review

build_rules: a stair has 17 risers or fewer between landings, risers of 16 to 17 cm, and the same riser all the way up a stair
a wall's coping follows its flight's pitch and runs level over a landing, a pier at every change of slope and at every end
a wall stands on what it retains or on the brink: never on a deck, never with a gap under it
walls meet towers and the keep square; doors sit square in their walls at their floor's level
one wall where there is one wall: nothing built in front of the curtain
painting_departures: slate roofs only on the great hall and the chapel (owner's pick, October 3); the keep, the kitchen, the solar, the stables, the barracks and the towers without spires keep flat roofs behind battlements
one fall on the axis under the gate terrace instead of two either side of the bridge: the water has one way out to the stream
the approach climbs a stone stair up the rock's south-east corner and runs along the ledge to the gate, instead of a straight causeway up the cliff
the keep's back rises out of the moat and the hall and the chapel are mirrored either side of it, where the painting has a hall on one side only
no cottage houses round the forecourt: the service buildings stand along the side walls, so the axis stays open
the gate drums stay flat with flags; only the corner towers and the keep carry spires (the painting gives every tower one)
the moat lies two metres down between built banks, held by a weir, rather than brimming at the foot of the walls

interiors.note: Every building the hero enters has a plan whose inside fits its outside: its rooms sit inside its walls, every door is one door seen from both sides at one floor level, every window lights a room (never a floor slab or a stair's underside), every chimney stands over a hearth and every upper floor has a stair that fits under its ceiling. Floors are given above the crown; doors are [x, z] on the wall's centre line.
rules: a door's head stays under the floor above it: a building door (2 wide, 4 high) needs 4.3 clear, so the bay of a building door has no loft over it unless the loft is 4.3 or more above the sill
straight stairs inside as outside: 17 risers or fewer to a flight, risers of 16 to 17 cm, at least 1 m wide, 2.1 m headroom under anything over them
the north range builds its own back wall against the curtain (it rises above the walk); the stables and barracks, lower than the walk, use the curtain as their back wall
a window sits within one storey: its sill above that storey's floor and its head under the next floor
